As per the demand of Respondent, parents of 1st petitioner had given a sum of Rs.80,000/- (Rupees Eighty Thousand Only) and 150 grams of gold to the respondent and performed the marriage at Bengaluru by spending Rs.6,00,000/-

They lived together for a period of 2 years.
1st Petitioner has served the respondent in all manner to uplift the family respect in the society and discharged her duties as a dutiful wife.
Thereafter 1st petitioner got pregnant.

Hence, she/1st Petitioner went to her parents'
house for delivery with the permission of respondent and she gave birth to 2 nd petitioner at her parent's house.
d) It is averred that, even after lapse of 5 years, respondent neither came to 1st Petitioner's parent's house nor took them/petitioners from 1 st Petitioner's parents house.
After making several panchayaths by the elders, respondent had made a house at Gowdanapalya.
She joined the Respondent at Gowdanapalya.
Respondent did not come to the said house properly and he failed to provide basic amenities to them.
Thereby Respondent totally neglected the petitioners.
Hence, she/ 1st Petitioner fallen sick.
Later, she came to know that respondent is having illicit relationship with one Vanitha.
When the 1st petitioner questioned the same respondent assaulted her physically and mentally and demanded her more dowry.
e) It is averred that, Respondent did not come to the house of the petitioners' months together.
The elders of the petitioners' family had made a panchayath, but the said panchayath not ended fruitfully.
Finally 1st petitioner was questioned about illegal relationship.
Thereafter the said Vanitha and her relative Ramakrishna were threatened the petitioners to kill them if they enters in this matter.
As such she lodged complaint against said Vanitha and Ramakrishna before the Subramanyapura Police Station.
The police have registered a case against them in Cr. No.296/2013 for the offences punishable under Sec.498A, 506 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
It is further averred that 1st petitioner also lodged complaint against the respondent before Kesturu police station, Maddur Taluk.
f) It is averred that, when the petitioners were in the above said house and without any fault of her,
respondent

behind her back filed the divorce petition against the 1st petitioner in M.C.No.
4412/2012 before the I Addl. Family Court at Bengaluru by making false and cooked up stories.

The petitioners are entirely depending on the 1st petitioner's parents.

h) It is averred that respondent is a car driver and having his own car.

He is doing travel business,
chit business, steel and bangles business in the name and style of 'Vanitha Enterprises' and he is also having landed properties at Maddur Taluk in the name of his father and earning a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- p.m..
It is averred that respondent is having good income and has leading luxurious life and totally neglected the petitioners from the last 9 years.
As such she filed this petition seeking maintenance from the respondent.
3) On service of notice, Respondent appeared through his counsel and filed his statement of objections by denying all the averments found in the petition except the relationship.
However, the respondent called upon the petitioner to prove the strict proof of the allegations made against him in the petition.
a) It is contested that, 1st petitioner without any reason abused him filthy language.
Petitioner's only intention is he/respondent has to reside at her parents' house.
The parents of the 1st petitioner also encouraged her/1st petitioner in ill- treating the respondent.
The amount of harassment meted out by him/respondent compelled him to call them as beasts in human form.
According to him 1st petitioner and her parents were very aggressive and rude when they talks.
Her intention is only to live with her parents.
b) It is contended that respondent with an intention to maintain cordial relationship, he has agreed to live in her parents house for some time.
But 1 st petitioner has not mended her ways.
She used to ill-treat the respondent.
She does not know the minimum duties and responsibilities as a loyal wife.
Whenever the respondent go to his village to see his parents, 1st petitioner used to pick up quarrel.
The life of respondent became miserable due to the acts of the 1st petitioner.
c) It is contended that, respondent is working as a car driver and he came from respectable family.
The 1st petitioner made an attempt to malign his name among his relatives and friends circle.
Thereafter he left the 1st petitioner's parents house.
After that some panchayaths were held, as per the advice of the panchayathdars, 1 st petitioner and respondent started living together in separate house at Bengaluru.
The parents of the 1st petitioner joined their matrimonial house.
Again Petitioner/she started galata with the support of her parents and her cousin brothers.
They harassed the respondent stating that, they would lodge a complaint if he left the house.
Due to this, the respondent become miserable and his mental incapacity was developed.
As such without alternative he left the house of 1 st petitioner's parents and joined his parents.
d) It is contended that he has paid rent and family expenses to the petitioner and child along with the parents of the 1st petitioner.
He is ready and wiling to take care of the petitioners.

Respondent tolerated all those thinking that the petitioner may mend her way one day or the other.
Later she started showing her true colour and also started harassing the respondent .
e) It is contended that there were several incompatibilities and misunderstanding between her and respondent.
Though the respondent trying to adjust with the 1st petitioner and her family as the things may change in future and for welfare of the child.
The 1st petitioner not mend her way and she has been caused intolerable harassment.
f) It is further contended that he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000 for the marriage and get jewelries to the petitioner.
However, the 1 st petitioner by influence of her parents and cousin brother mental agony was intensified.
As such he left the house.
It is contended that he has filed divorce petition against the 1 st petitioner in MC No.4412/2012.
However, due to intervention of the elders, 1st petitioner approached the respondent to settle the issues amicable and expressed her willing to stay with him.
As such he withdraw the said petition.
g) It is contended that respondent provide shelter to the petitioners at his native place and the 1st petitioner residing in the said house and all the expenses were borne by the respondent.
Though the 1st petitioner aware that the respondent has already got married one Smt. Vanitha.
Which was his love marriage.
However, the family of the respondent was not accepted the said marriage.
As such with the consent of Smt. Vanitha and respondent the family members made the marriage of the 1st petitioner and respondent, the 1st petitioner is the second wife of the respondent.
He has male child from first marriage.

Though the 1st petitioner knowing all these facts intentionally spoiled the life of respondent and the respondent being the daily waged car driver and not in a position to pay the monthly maintenance of Rs.30,000/- as claimed by the 1 st petitioner.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with heavy costs.

18) Admittedly, Respondent in his cross-examination in M.C. No. 4412/2012 deposed before the court that, he do not know Smt. Vanitha and Bharath. However all of a sudden before filing objections to the present petition he/respondent states that Smt. Vanitha is his 1st wife and he married her in the year 1998. If Smt. Vanitha is his 1st wife, 1st Petitioner knowing that he is the husband of Smt Vanitha and they have got married in the year 1998 itself as per the respondent's version, definitely he would have state the same in the earlier petition.
Even petitioner repeatedly states that, respondent has illicit relationship with One Smt. Vanitha, why he keep quite till filing of objections and what-else prohibited him is not forth coming.
On the otherhand Respondent by hiding the said fact before the Hon'ble Family court he ought to have deceived the 1 st Petitioner right of maintenance.
This is nothing but a cruelty on the 1st Petitioner by the Respondent.

Hence without discussing further, this court is of the opinion that the respondent inflicted the domestic violence against the 1st petitioner and also neglected the petitioners for a period of 9 years as stated by the 1 st petitioner in her petition.
Hence, this point No.1 answers in the affirmative for the Petitioner.

sentences.text: Hence an adverse inference can be drawn against him under section 114(g) of Indian Evidence Act that, though he has sufficient income, failed to furnish the same in order to avoid maintenance to the Petitioner.
Therefore it is clear that petitioner is entitled for maintenance.
The object of providing maintenance is to achieve social purpose i.e., to prevent vagrancy and destitution.

Having regard to the circumstance of the case and high cost of living and requirements fo the petitioners and capacity of the respondent to pay the maintenance this court is of the opinion that if a sum of Rs.3,000/- to the 1st petitioner and Rs.2,000/- to the 2nd petitioner is fixed as monthly maintenance it would serve the ends of justice.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitle for monthly maintenance of Rs.6,000/- from the respondent from the date of Petition.
Hence this point No.2 answers in the partly affirmative for the Petitioner.

Hence an adverse inference can be drawn against him under section 114(g) of Indian Evidence Act that, though he has sufficient income, failed to furnish the same in order to avoid maintenance to the Petitioner.
Therefore it is clear that petitioner is entitled for maintenance.
The object of providing maintenance is to achieve social purpose i.e., to prevent vagrancy and destitution.
Having regard to the circumstance of the case and high cost of living and requirements fo the petitioners and capacity of the respondent to pay the maintenance this court is of the opinion that if a sum of Rs.3,000/- to the 1st petitioner and Rs.2,000/- to the 2nd petitioner is fixed as monthly maintenance it would serve the ends of justice.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitle for monthly maintenance of Rs.6,000/- from the respondent from the date of Petition.

In view of the forgoing reasons this court proceed to pass the following:-
::ORDER::
The Petition filed by the petitioner under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is allowed in part.
It is directed to the respondent not to commit any act of domestic violence against the Petitioners.
It is directed to the respondent to pay monthly maintenance of Rs. 3,000/- (Rupees Three Thousand Only) to the 1st Petitioner and 2,000/-(Rupees Two Thousand Only)
to the 2nd Petitioner from the date of Petition to till 1st Petitioner got remarried or her lifetime which ever is earlier and 2nd petitioner attains majority.
It is directed to the respondent to pay compensation of Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Only) to 1st Petitioner.
It is directed to the respondent to get it repair the house of 1st Petitioner within 6 months from the date of order of this court.
In case if he fails to repair it, then he is liable to pay Rs.5,000/-(Rupees Five Thousand Only) to the 1st petitioner every month towards rent.
By considering the relationship of the parties, cost not imposed.
Office is hereby directed to furnish the copy of this order free of cost to the petitioner.
